status: Execution plan frozen for foundation batch; later paid plans must freeze exact samples/model bindings before launch. No product budget or target-contract edits.
primaryObjective: Demonstrate low overhead on the actual Loom path with acceptable task quality; source absorption is subordinate to that objective.

candidate.ordinaryReply: Explicit per-Run native-final-text mode; Host binds original Worker identity, unique delivered target and frozen causal sequence. Provider-specific adapter proves the current complete final.
candidate.otherActions: Progress, attachments, multiple targets, Task and memory remain explicit existing actions.
candidate.authority: Kernel retains event, cursor, ACK, stale hold, idempotency and final marker authority; Run end and Activation completion remain separate.
candidate.history: Preserve continuous native sessions; disable provider auto memory on every benchmark launch. Routine success receipts need not be injected into model history.
candidate.scope: This foundation batch adds laboratory submission tests and free CLI prototypes only, not production enabling.

stages.work: Clarify workload without changing old evidence; retain immutable artifact bytes/hash before evaluating every future round; account per-response usage once.
stages.exit: Free adversarial evaluator/retention/accounting tests pass; historical v2 scores unchanged.

stages.work: Native final identity and Worker failure boundaries; actual installed Pi/Kimi with loopback fake provider.
stages.exit: Two continuous turns, real file tools and Worker publications; negative final evidence rejected; usage/memory/process cleanup audited. No paid-quality claim.

stages.work: Small opt-in actual AgentHost/Kernel integration for already-proven providers; preserve other transports.
stages.exit: TDD and real installed CLI/fake-provider through actual scheduler including busy follow-up, cancellation and unknown-result hold. Source implementation is not deployment acceptance.

stages.work: Paid native-normalized single-instance work across five CLIs and multiple approved models.
stages.exit: Preregistered complete paired trajectories, quality and all costs; per-CLI/model conclusions. An unavailable CLI is marked unavailable and does not cancel other providers.

stages.work: Two sessions exchanging public replies against a native manual-relay baseline; three instances only after two-instance results.
stages.exit: All participants and failed attempts counted; independent artifact acceptance and real reviewer contribution. Herdr claim requires actual Herdr baseline.

stages.work: Narrow phase4 UI replacement and proven Raft interaction gaps.
stages.exit: After cost decision, real UI/API acceptance plus required backup/restart; no whole-server replacement.

measurementRules: Compare same CLI/model/effort, same initial artifacts and business instructions; separate continuous sessions per arm; count all native tool and model work.
Freeze workload, sample count, paired order, budgets and stop behavior before paid requests. Counterbalance launch order across preregistered repeats; retain cache-order confounding.
Report whole task and planned late window, first-generation input delta, cached/uncached input, output, provider reasoning semantics, latency, business/protocol generations and any unknown usage.
Report quality and cost together including unsuccessful attempts. Do not keep rerunning until pass or drop failed pairs; censored/incomplete runs have no full-task multiplier.
Quality errors continue through the frozen valid task sequence without oracle feedback. Authentication, model binding, isolation, usage integrity and budget errors stop that batch.
Free scripted providers prove transport and invariants only, never real model quality or cost.
Contract section6 remains the numeric engineering gate. Passing it alone does not establish the owner near-native economic objective; sustained1.63x cannot be called product success.
Price/bill and reported token ratios are distinct. Unknown provider usage is not zero; cumulative session cost is counted once, not summed each resume.
decisions: If actual product integration adds mandatory communication generations or redundant replay, stop expanding paid matrix and fix that owner.
If fixed protocol overhead is small but business paths vary, use the frozen repetitions rather than more prompt instructions.
If single-instance works but collaboration exceeds cost, investigate wakes and routing before rewriting single-instance transport.
Do not absorb an upstream subsystem solely because source became available; require a concrete gap and suitable license/provenance before code adoption.
raftScope: Use failure scenarios as reference; no source copied. Preserve existing owner/continuous sessions. Do not adopt cross-channel Agent-global lane, automatic session recycle, cloud tenant stack or new UI architecture.
remainingDecision: No new arbitrary near-native percentage or statistical confidence claim is introduced here; acceptance criteria for each paid batch must be explicit before it starts, and an uncertain observation stays inconclusive.
